📚 Enterprise Knowledge Assistant — Ask Your Documents Anything, Get Cited Answers Only

LlamaIndex + Cognee + Qdrant + Ollama: a fully local RAG chatbot over 11 enterprise HR/policy PDFs. Every answer is synthesized only from retrieved evidence — a hybrid retriever fuses semantic vector search, BM25 keyword search and knowledge-graph relationships; a calibrated evidence gate refuses to answer before the LLM is ever called when the documents don't support it; and every claim carries filenames from the real corpus. No cloud LLM APIs for the knowledge layer, no Docker, no paid vector DB — the whole stack runs on one Windows machine.

The 30-second pitch

Enterprise knowledge lives in PDFs nobody reads. An employee asks "How many annual leave days do I get?" and someone has to open four documents, find the tenure table, and paraphrase it — every single time. Meanwhile, if you ask a normal chatbot, it happily invents a plausible-sounding policy that exists nowhere.

This project turns the document folder into an assistant that can only tell the truth — or say "I don't know". Documents are ingested once by Cognee, which chunks them, extracts entities and relationships into a knowledge graph, and embeds everything into a local Qdrant vector store. At question time a hybrid retriever runs three legs in parallel — semantic vector search, BM25 keyword search, and graph-triplet search — fuses the two chunk legs with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, and hands the evidence to a LlamaIndex pipeline with a grounded prompt. Before the LLM even runs, an evidence gate checks the best cosine similarity against a data-calibrated threshold: thin evidence → instant refusal, zero hallucination risk. Answers cite real filenames, and a debug panel exposes the entire evidence chain. The LLM is Ollama — local qwen3:8b or cloud gpt-oss:120b — so nothing proprietary is involved end-to-end.

The line that matters: grounding isn't a prompt instruction — it's a mechanical gate plus cited evidence, measured by a 58-question evaluation with quality gates that fail the build.

The one-line principle

🚪 Refuse before you generate

The evidence gate checks the best retrieved cosine score against a calibrated threshold (0.55) before any LLM call. Unrelated questions (World Cup, cookies, Tesla) score ≤ 0.53 and are refused mechanically — a hallucinated answer is impossible by construction, not by hoping the prompt behaves.

🧬 Three legs beat one

Vector search finds meaning, BM25 finds exact terms (policy IDs like ACME-HR-002), the graph finds relationships (what governs what). RRF fusion ranks by agreement — rank-only math, no score normalization — and every hit records which legs found it.

📏 Measure, don't assume

A 58-question golden dataset (factual, paraphrase, multi-hop, distractor, unsupported) is scored on refusal accuracy, correctness, citations, context relevance and LLM-judged faithfulness. quality_gates.yaml fails the run (exit 1) when a metric drops — CI-ready honesty.

The signal: the metrics that measure retrieval (citations 0.96, context relevance 0.94) are excellent — the metrics that measure generation honesty (faithfulness 0.775, refusal 0.914) are the improvement backlog, and the dashboard says so out loud instead of hiding it. That's what a production RAG eval loop looks like: measure, expose the weak metric, fix the layer that's actually weak.

What is this project?

The Enterprise Knowledge Assistant is a chat window over your document folder that answers questions about company policies — annual leave, remote work, expenses, security — with answers that can only come from those documents, each one stamped with the file it came from.

You simply:

  1. Open the app — the sidebar shows the 11 indexed policy PDFs and live service health
  2. Type a question like "How many annual leave days do employees receive?"
  3. Get a grounded answer with a Sources list of real filenames
  4. Ask something the documents don't cover — get an honest "could not be found" instead of a guess

Think of it as a librarian who has memorized every page but refuses to speak a single sentence that isn't written in one of the books — and always tells you which book, every time.

What does the app look like?

The screenshots below are from a real run on this machine. The main area is a clean chat; every control lives in the sidebar.

First launch — documents and health at a glance

The sidebar lists all 11 indexed documents (the bundled HR corpus). Below it, the System Status panel runs real health checks — local Ollama daemon, the embedding model, Ollama Cloud reachability, Qdrant, the Cognee graph (1,604 nodes / 4,605 relationships) and the vector index (131 chunks). Six green lines mean everything is ready; these are live probes, not placeholders.

A grounded answer, with receipts

Asking "How many annual leave days do employees receive?" returns the tenure-based PTO table from the policy text — 15 days for 0–2 years, up to 30 for 11+ — with the citation marker 【3】 pointing at the evidence. The Sources expander lists the exact corpus files the answer was built from: never invented names, never fake page numbers.

The unknown question — no fabrication

Ask about a private jet travel policy (which doesn't exist) and the assistant explains — using only retrieved context — that the documents cover economy/business air travel and per-diem rules but contain nothing about private jets. It declines rather than invents. This is the evaluation suite's unsupported category, and the system is built so this behavior is the default, not a lucky day.

Why this matters: a chatbot that invents policy is worse than no chatbot — employees act on wrong answers. The two layers that prevent it (the mechanical evidence gate and the grounded prompt) are both unit-tested; the screenshot above is the happy path of that guarantee.

Peek behind the curtain (debug mode)

Flip Developer / debug mode in the sidebar and every answer carries its full evidence chain: the retrieval strategy, each vector hit with its cosine score, the BM25 keyword ranking, the RRF fusion order the LLM actually saw, and the graph triplets that contributed.

The fusion section is the heart of hybrid retrieval: each fused chunk shows its RRF score and which legs found it — "vector+bm25 ✔" means both retrieval methods agreed the chunk was relevant. Below that, the Graph Entities / Relationships section shows the actual knowledge-graph triplets retrieved for the question, e.g. onboarding policy ──is_a──> policy and travel expenses ──includes_section──> air travel.

The knowledge graph — see what the AI learned

The sidebar's Knowledge graph view section explains the map and opens it in a new browser tab: an interactive diagram of the 500 nodes / 1,394 edges Cognee extracted from your documents — documents, chunks, entities and types laid out in columns.

In the graph page you can search ("remote work" jumps straight to the matching nodes), switch between Story / Flow / Force layouts, hover a dot for its inspector panel — showing the source chunk it was extracted from, the pipeline that created it, and its relationship counts — and open the Schema tab to see the node kinds and how they connect.

Everything configurable lives in the sidebar

Configuration shows the active LLM, embedding model and Top-K. Retrieval options switches between hybrid (all three legs) and vector (chunks only). Example questions are click-to-copy prompts tagged by which retrieval strength they exercise — [semantic], [keyword], [graph] and [refusal].

The 4-step workflow

1

Start the services

Ollama (embeddings), Qdrant (vectors) — then the app. One script verifies all of it.

Order matters: the app talks to Qdrant and Ollama lazily, so both must be up first. scripts\check_services.py prints a real ✅/❌ line per service; the sidebar's System Status panel shows the same checks live. First-time setup (one command each) is in the Technical Guide.

The one rule that matters: answers can only be as good as the index behind them. If you add or edit documents, press Process documents (or run the ingest script) — a SHA-256 hash ledger skips everything already processed, so re-ingestion is cheap and idempotent.
2

Ask a question

The hybrid retriever fans out to three legs and fuses the results by agreement.

Your question is embedded and searched semantically (Qdrant), matched keyword-exactly (BM25), and used to find related graph triplets. Each leg fetches 12 candidates before fusion — deliberately deeper than the final Top-8, because a chunk ranked 6th by meaning and 10th by keywords can fuse to rank 3; truncating early would drop exactly the best evidence. That behavior was measured, not guessed (see the Technical Guide).

Retrieval legFindsExample strength
🔎 Vector (Qdrant)paraphrases and meaning"annual leave days" → PTO accrual table
🔤 BM25 (keyword)exact IDs and statutory terms"policy ACME-HR-002" → that exact policy
🕸️ Graph (Cognee)relationships between concepts"how are remote work and security related?"
3

The gate decides

Thin evidence → instant, honest refusal. Enough evidence → grounded generation.

If the best retrieved score is below the calibrated threshold, you immediately get "I don't have enough evidence in the provided documents to answer this question reliably." — and the LLM was never called. If evidence clears the bar, the LLM sees only numbered evidence blocks and a prompt that says: use only this, preserve exact numbers, cite sources, or say the information could not be found.

4

Read the answer, check the sources

Every answer carries real filenames; debug mode shows the full evidence chain.

Citations are built from retrieved node metadata — never from the LLM's output — so a source line means a chunk from that file was actually in the context. Try the sample questions in the sidebar: the semantic, keyword, graph and refusal examples each showcase a different layer of the system.

Try it yourself: start Qdrant, start the app, and click the first example question. The whole demo runs on your machine — no account, no API key for the knowledge layer.

Tips for best results

Do
  • Use the example questions first — they're verified against this corpus and tagged by retrieval leg
  • Watch the Sources expander — if an answer surprises you, the filenames tell you where it came from
  • Turn on debug mode when curious — you'll see exactly why an answer was or wasn't given
  • Process documents after adding files — the hash ledger makes re-runs fast
Avoid
  • Don't ask cross-document arithmetic ("sum all PTO across policies") — retrieval fetches passages, not spreadsheets
  • Don't expect answers about documents that aren't indexed — check the sidebar list
  • Don't run two apps/scripts against the graph simultaneously — the graph DB takes an exclusive file lock (Error 33)
  • Don't trust a topic the sources don't cover — that's the point; the app will say so itself

Frequently asked questions

Does it ever make things up?

The design makes that the hardest thing to do, not the easiest. Unrelated questions are refused before the LLM runs; answerable questions are generated from a prompt that forbids invention and requires citations. The 58-question evaluation includes a whole unsupported category to keep that promise honest — and where the LLM still drifts beyond evidence, the faithfulness metric exposes it (that's the 77.5% you see on the dashboard).

Is my data going to the cloud?

No. Documents, chunks, embeddings and the graph never leave your machine. The only optional outbound call is the chat LLM if you choose OLLAMA_PROVIDER=cloud — questions and retrieved context go to Ollama Cloud for stronger answers; switch to local and even that stays on your box.

Why filenames instead of page numbers in citations?

Cognee's chunks don't carry page metadata, and the project refuses to fabricate page numbers it doesn't have — the same grounding principle applied to its own UI. Per-page citations are on the roadmap once chunk metadata carries them.

What happens if Qdrant or Ollama is down?

The sidebar flags it in red, and if you ask anyway, the app diagnoses the failure with real probes and tells you which service to start — not a raw stack trace. The retrieval legs also degrade independently: if the graph leg fails, chunk evidence still answers, with the failure recorded in the debug panel.

System overview

The app is a Streamlit UI over a LlamaIndex query engine, backed by two stores: a Qdrant collection of 131 embedded chunks and a Cognee knowledge graph (1,604 nodes / 4,605 relationships). Ingestion has a single authoritative path — Cognee does chunking, entity/ relationship extraction, embeddings and vector insertion; nothing re-implements that. Query time is a three-legged hybrid retriever, an RRF fuser, a pre-LLM evidence gate, and a grounded prompt sent to an Ollama LLM through one provider interface.

Ingestion: the single path through Cognee

All processing funnels through app/knowledge/cognee_manager.py — the app never re-implements chunking, embedding or insertion. Documents are hashed (SHA-256) first; the ledger data/metadata/ingested.json makes re-runs skip everything unchanged. Cognee's LLM and embedding providers and its Qdrant adapter are configured programmatically from the same .env values the rest of the app uses — one source of configuration. 

# scripts/ingest_corpus.py (first run ~20-30 min for 11 PDFs on cloud LLM)
manager = DocumentManager(settings.document_dir, settings.metadata_dir)
paths   = [Path(m.source_path) for m in manager.inventory()]   # inventory w/ hashes
result  = CognifyManager(settings).ingest_all(paths)
# → {"processed": 11, "skipped_duplicates": 0}   second run: {"new": 0, "skipped_duplicates": 11}
# Cognee: chunk (800/100) → entity+relationship extraction (LLM) → summaries
#         → embeddings (local nomic-embed-text) → Qdrant upsert (max 30 concurrent)
Real corpus numbers: the bundled 11-PDF corpus yields 131 embedded chunks, a 1,604-node / 4,605-relationship graph, and 6 Qdrant collections (chunks, entities, edges, entity types, documents, summaries). The upload button in the sidebar routes through the same manager with filename sanitization (§53: allowlist, no path traversal).

The three retrieval legs

Each leg is its own class; HybridRetriever.retrieve() composes them and never merges their evidence kinds — chunk hits and graph triplets travel as separate lists all the way to the prompt, where they become [1]…[n] and [G1]…[Gn] blocks.

Class (file)BackendWhy it exists
VectorRetriever
retrieval/vector_retriever.py		 Qdrant DocumentChunk_text, cosine, 768-dim semantic matches with real chunk→document provenance from the Cognee graph
BM25Retriever
retrieval/bm25_retriever.py		 pure-Python rank-bm25, index built once per process exact terminology the embedder is weak on — ACME-HR-002, statutory phrases
GraphRetriever
retrieval/graph_retriever.py		 Cognee graph (Ladybug store), triplet search relationship questions — "which policy governs what" — vector search can't answer 
# hybrid_retriever.py — the depth-12 leg fetch (measured, not guessed)
leg_depth = max(top_k, 12)          # RRF ranks legs independently; a chunk at
vector_hits = self._vector.retrieve(query, top_k=leg_depth)   # vector-rank 6 +
bm25_hits   = self._bm25.retrieve(query, top_k=leg_depth)     # bm25-rank 10 fuses
fused       = rrf_fuse(vector_hits, bm25_hits)[:top_k]        # to rank 3 — a naive
# top-8 truncation per leg dropped it entirely (measured 2026-09-09, PTO chunk)

RRF fusion and the evidence gate

Fusion is rank-only — score(d) = Σ 1/(60 + rank) — so BM25 magnitudes (≈8–13) and cosine similarities (≈0.5–0.75) never need normalizing. Dedupe is by chunk_id, and every fused hit records contributed_by, which the debug panel and the evaluator both read. The gate then makes the refusal mechanical: 

# llamaindex_engine.answer() — enforcement before generation
evidence   = self.retriever.retrieve(query, top_k=top_k)
best_score = max((h.score for h in evidence.vector_hits), default=None)
decision   = self.gate.check(best_score)          # threshold 0.55 (calibrated)
if not decision.allowed:
    return RetrievalResult(answer=REFUSAL_MESSAGE, refused=True, ...)
# → "I don't have enough evidence in the provided documents to answer
#    this question reliably."  — LLM never called

# calibration (scripts/probe_scores.py, real corpus):
#   known questions:   0.627 – 0.737   (6 probes)
#   unrelated:         0.453 – 0.538   (World Cup, cookies, Tesla, Louvre)
#   lexical trap:      0.638  "private jet travel policy" — passes gate ON PURPOSE
Two layers, deliberately: the gate handles the mechanical case (nothing related in the index). The lexically-overlapping trap (0.638 > 0.55) is caught by the semantic layer — the grounded prompt instructs "if the context does not contain enough information, say so" — and both layers have their own tests. The gate is conservative by design: graph triplets can't rescue a low vector score because unrelated queries retrieve unrelated triplets anyway.

The grounded prompt (verbatim from the code)

GROUNDED_PROMPT = """\
Answer the user's question using only the provided enterprise
knowledge context.

If the context does not contain enough information to answer,
say that the information could not be found in the available
documents.

Do not invent facts, policies, numbers, dates, sources, or page
numbers.

Preserve exact numbers and dates from the evidence.

When multiple documents provide evidence, distinguish them clearly.

Provide source citations for claims supported by retrieved evidence.
"""

The engine appends numbered evidence blocks ([1] … (source: file.pdf), [G1] … (source: knowledge graph)) and the question. The LLM's job is constrained to synthesis over supplied context — every other behavior is the gate's, the retriever's, or the citation builder's, and each of those is deterministic code.

LLM providers: local vs cloud behind one interface

OLLAMA_PROVIDERChat modelEmbeddingsNotes
local qwen3:8b on localhost:11434 nomic-embed-text (local daemon) zero external calls; weaker long-form answers
cloud gpt-oss:120b via https://ollama.com/api + API key nomic-embed-text (local daemon) stronger synthesis; 429 backoff handled; needs OLLAMA_API_KEY
Why embeddings are always local: the Ollama cloud plan carries no embedding models — /api/embed returns 401 — so the embedding leg pins to the local daemon. The provider split lives in app/llm/providers/; the engine never sees which one is active.

Evaluation harness and quality gates

data/eval/golden_dataset.jsonl holds 58 manually verified Q/A pairs across factual · terminology · paraphrase · multi_hop · distractor · unsupported · ambiguous with difficulty tags; tests/test_golden_dataset.py enforces structural integrity. The runner (scripts/evaluate_rag.py) scores each question on five metrics — including a custom strict LLM-judge for faithfulness via the same Ollama provider (judge errors are recorded, never silently scored as failures) — and writes evaluation/results.json. 

python scripts\evaluate_rag.py                # full 58-question run, LLM-judged (~25 min)
python scripts\evaluate_rag.py --limit 6      # smoke run
python scripts\evaluate_rag.py --skip-judge   # mechanical metrics only
python scripts\evaluate_rag.py --category unsupported
Metric (gate)baseline_v2 · 58 questionsGateVerdict
citation_accuracy (≥ 0.90)0.96passprovenance map works
context_relevance (≥ 0.80)0.94passretrieval precision strong
answer_correctness (≥ 0.80)0.84passkeyword-verified
refusal_accuracy (= 1.00)0.914fail2 unsupported answered with unrecognized "not provided" phrasing
faithfulness (≥ 0.85)0.775failLLM drifts beyond evidence on multi-hop

Median latency 21.98 s, p95 31.39 s per question (cloud LLM). check_quality_gates() exits 1 on any gate failure — CI-ready. The failures are known and documented: the first baseline exposed them, and the fix belongs to the generation layer (better synthesis discipline), not to loosening thresholds.

Gate philosophy: gates are config (data/eval/quality_gates.yaml), not code — adjust them after establishing a baseline, never to mask a failure. Lowering the faithfulness gate to make the run green would be hiding the only metric that measures honesty.

Configuration (.env-driven, validated at boot)

OLLAMA_PROVIDER=cloud            # local | cloud
OLLAMA_BASE_URL=http://localhost:11434

OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL=nomic-embed-text          # local daemon, always
QDRANT_URL=http://localhost:6333
QDRANT_COLLECTION=enterprise_documents
TOP_K=8                          # fused evidence blocks per query
EVIDENCE_MIN_SCORE=0.55          # gate threshold (calibrated)
CHUNK_SIZE=800  CHUNK_OVERLAP=100
DATA_DIR=./data  DOCUMENT_DIR=./data/documents  METADATA_DIR=./data/metadata
LOG_LEVEL=INFO

Every key maps to exactly one typed field on the frozen Settings dataclass (app/config/settings.py); invalid values raise ConfigurationError at startup — the app fails fast instead of misbehaving mid-session.

CLI equivalent: python scripts\ask_question.py answers from the existing index in a fresh process — proving persistence (no re-ingestion, no rebuild). Handy for smoke-testing without the UI.

Design decisions worth knowing

  • Refusal by construction, not instruction — the gate runs before generation, so the refusal doesn't depend on the LLM obeying. The prompt is the second layer, not the first.
  • Rank-only fusion (RRF k=60) — avoids the normalization trap entirely; BM25 scores and cosine similarities never meet in the same arithmetic.
  • Leg depth 12 > top_k — measured: deep per-leg candidate pools promote cross-leg agreement; naive top-k truncation dropped a chunk that fused to rank 3.
  • Graph triplets are never fused into chunks — different evidence kind, own provenance, own [G*] blocks; the engine renders them separately so citations stay honest.
  • Provenance over convenience — filenames come from Cognee's graph-derived metadata; page numbers are omitted (not invented) because chunks carry none.
  • Real health, real errors — the sidebar reuses check_services.py; UI errors are diagnosed by actual probes before a friendly message is chosen; leg failures degrade with recorded errors, never silently.
  • Evaluation is part of the definition of done — the golden dataset, judge, and gates are test-enforced; gates fail the build, and the first baseline's two failures are documented backlog, not hidden.

Glossary — every technical term in this guide

Every technical term that appears in the Elevator Pitch, Non-Technical Guide, and Technical Guide — expanded to its full form, explained in plain English, and located in this project. Terms are grouped by theme so you can jump to the area you need.

🔍 Retrieval & ranking

TermExpansionWhat It MeansWhere in This Project
RAGRetrieval-Augmented GenerationFetch relevant passages first, then have the LLM write the answer only from them — instead of from its training memory.The entire app pattern: HybridRetriever → context blocks → grounded prompt → LLM.
Hybrid RetrievalHybrid SearchCombining semantic (vector) and lexical (keyword) search so meaning-matches and exact-term matches both surface.HybridRetriever — vector + BM25 legs, fused by RRF; this project adds the graph leg on top.
BM25Best Match 25 (ranking function)The classic keyword-scoring algorithm — rewards exact term matches with saturation and length normalization.BM25Retriever over the same 131 chunks; the reason "policy ACME-HR-002" ranks first.
RRFReciprocal Rank FusionCombine ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank) per list — rank-only, so different score scales never need normalizing.fusion.py, k=60; dedupes by chunk_id and records contributed_by.
Top-KTop-K RetrievalHow many evidence chunks are passed to the LLM as context.TOP_K=8 in .env; legs fetch 12 deep before truncation.
Chunk / ChunkingText ChunkingSplitting documents into overlapping passages small enough to embed and retrieve precisely.Cognee chunks at 800 chars / 100 overlap → 131 chunks for 11 PDFs.
EmbeddingVector EmbeddingA numeric vector representing a passage's meaning, so "similar meaning" becomes "nearby point".nomic-embed-text, 768 dimensions, always via the local Ollama daemon.
Re-rankerCross-Encoder Re-rankerA second-stage model that re-scores retrieved candidates for precision.Deliberately deferred: retrieval metrics (0.94/0.96) show precision is not the weak layer — faithfulness is.

Ollama CloudOllama Cloud (ollama.com)Hosted Ollama with larger models; chat only — no embedding models on this plan.gpt-oss:120b for generation; key only in .env.
qwen3:8b / gpt-oss:120bOpen-weight chat modelsThe synthesis engines; swap by changing one env var.OLLAMA_LLM_MODEL; provider classes in app/llm/providers/.
nomic-embed-textNomic Embed Text (embedding model)768-dimension embedding model; the only embedding leg in the system.Local daemon; used by Cognee at ingest and by the retriever at query time.
StreamlitStreamlit (Python UI framework)Rapid data-app UI in pure Python.The whole interface — chat, sidebar, debug panel — in app/ui/.
Streamlit Session Statest.session_statePer-browser-tab memory; holds chat history, cached engines, health results.One engine per (settings, strategy); health checks cached stale-while-revalidate.
pytestpytest (test framework)The automated test suite — 30 tests, hermetic + service-backed.tests/; service-backed tests skip (not fail) when services are down.

🏢 Domain concepts

TermExpansionWhat It MeansWhere in This Project
CorpusDocument CorpusThe collection of documents the assistant knows about.11 HR/policy PDFs in data/documents/.
Chunk IDChunk Identifier (UUID)The stable identifier of one retrieved passage — used for dedupe and eval attribution.Shown in the debug panel for every vector/BM25/RRF hit.
CitationSource CitationThe filename (and page, when real metadata exists) behind a claim.Built from node metadata only — never from LLM output; shown in the Sources expander.
Policy IDPolicy Identifier (e.g. ACME-HR-002)Exact document codes that keyword search handles better than embeddings.The [keyword] example question showcases the BM25 leg.
Multi-hopMulti-Hop Question (eval category)Questions needing evidence from two+ documents combined.Golden category; where the faithfulness backlog was measured.
PTOPaid Time OffAnnual leave — the corpus's flagship example (tiered by tenure: 15/20/25/30 days).The demo question; the RRF depth-12 fix was measured on a PTO chunk.
Cross-references: retrieval-leg details and the gate's calibration live in the Technical Guide; the walkthrough of real answers and the debug panel in the Non-Technical Guide; the numbers cited here come from evaluation/baseline_v2/results.json — every term above is used somewhere in those tabs — nothing here is decoration.
